analysis.title: Alphabet Inc. Assume Coverage with a Neutral and a Focus on Google Cloud
key_insights: UBS assumes coverage of Alphabet (GOOG/GOOGL) at an unchanged Neutral rating. The price target is cut to $320 from $380, based on 17x CY28E GAAP EPS of $18.86, in line with the peer group median.

The stock trades at 16x 2027E GAAP EPS, is down 6% YTD and down 26% from its May highs. UBS calls this reasonable but not compelling, because sentiment is already mixed and the near-term catalyst path (competitive model market, slowing core Search growth, Google Cloud margin pressure) is hard.

Google Cloud is 28% of revenue but drives 66% of y/y revenue growth. UBS expects it to exceed the core Search business in scale in 3Q28. UBS is shifting its research focus from Search and ad checks to Gemini competitiveness and Google Cloud.

Google Cloud revenue grew 103% in 3Q26, a 21-point acceleration, but fell short of investor expectations. UBS suggests frontier lab exposure and mix as a possible cause, along with capacity timing, token optimization and Gemini share shifts. It does not attribute the miss to weak enterprise demand.

UBS estimates direct TPU sales of $77B in 2027 and $125B in 2028. That is 30% of its 2027 Google Cloud revenue estimate ($254B) and 38% of 2028 ($325B). Ex-TPU Google Cloud growth would be 69% in 2026, 78% in 2027 and 14% in 2028. TPU sales are also a likely source of margin pressure.

UBS cuts its 4Q26 Google Cloud growth estimate to 111% from 128% and its 2027 estimate to 125% from 169%. The Street is at 109% for 4Q26 and 96% for 2027. UBS lowers its 2027 Google Cloud operating margin assumption to 28% from 30%, citing the mix of TPU sales and third-party capacity.

UBS cuts its 2027 capex estimate to $340B from $375B. The Street consensus is $328B, and UBS thinks the investor view may be $350B+. 2026 capex guidance is $195-205B, up from $91.4B in 2025. FCF was -$9B in 3Q26, and UBS expects Google to need external financing in 2027, mostly debt, with a low but non-zero chance of an equity raise.

Gemini 4 Carbon scored 60 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index and Argon scored 50. Anthropic's Fable 5.2 scored 65, so Gemini still trails the leader. On the Coding Agent Index, Carbon scored 55. Carbon costs $5.48 per task, below the two leaders.

Enterprise checks show Gemini as a clear #3 behind OpenAI and Anthropic. An AI-native customer saw Argon trail Fable and Astra by 15-25% on frontier workloads. Gemini wins on cost per outcome for high-volume classification, long-context and multimodal work. Some customers expect Gemini's share to rise, while others cut it or churned off it.

UBS Evidence Lab found Gemini use fell from 46% of respondents in Oct 2025 to 38% in March 2026. The Gemini app passed 1 billion MAUs at the end of 3Q26, up from 950M at the end of 2Q26, and growth is leveling off.

Google rents third-party capacity from SpaceX: a three-year deal at $920M per month for 110,000 Nvidia GPUs. It came online at the end of 3Q26, and Google guided to Google Cloud margin headwinds in 4Q26. Amazon's CEO said neoclouds run about 3,500 bps worse in operating margin than long-leased data centers.

UBS is not a 'capacity doomer'. Its data center checks say Google and peers are powering through go-live constraints. Political scrutiny after the midterms mainly affects new approvals from 2028 on, not construction already under way.

Google Cloud GAAP operating margin was 36% in 3Q26, up from 21% a year earlier. Core Search grew 12% in 3Q26 against a Street bogey of 15%, and Google guided to continued FX headwinds and tough compares in 4Q26. Non-Cloud segments grew 11%.

Google Cloud distribution is limited because closed Gemini models are not sold through AWS Bedrock or Microsoft Foundry. OpenAI models and Codex became available through Google Cloud (private preview) on Oct 21, 2026, a possible 2027 catalyst.
UBS scenario values: $500 upside (23x on $22.24 CY28E EPS), $320 base (17x on $18.86) and $160 downside (10x on $16.73). Forecast stock return is 9.7% against a market return assumption of 9.9%.

market_movers.rationale: UBS assumes coverage at Neutral and lowers the price target from $380 to $320, using 17x CY28E GAAP EPS of $18.86. Risks are Search deceleration, Cloud margin pressure, and the capex and negative FCF ramp.
Same call as GOOGL: Neutral with a $320 target, down from $380. UBS sees the stock at 16x 2027E EPS as reasonable but not compelling.

sector_views.rationale: Mixed sentiment, slowing core Search, a competitive AI model market and Google Cloud margin pressure offset accelerating Cloud revenue and the TPU ramp.

earnings_insights: 3Q26 (reported): Google Cloud revenue grew 103% y/y, a 21-point acceleration, but missed the Street growth expectation. Sequential dollar growth was $5.94B vs $4.7B in 2Q26.

3Q26 (reported): core Search grew 12% vs a Street bogey of 15%, despite the strongest query growth in five years. Google cited FX, lower AI Mode monetization, vertical factors and European regulation.
3Q26 (reported): Google Cloud GAAP operating margin was 36% vs 21% a year earlier. FCF was -$9B, with $265B in cash and securities and $125B of long-term debt at quarter end.
UBS 4Q26 Google Cloud estimate (forecast): 111% revenue growth, implying $6.5B in sequential adds. The Street consensus is 109% (implying $9.5B in sequential adds). The prior UBS team was at 128%.
UBS 2027 Google Cloud estimate (forecast): 125% growth to $254B. The Street is at 96%, and the prior UBS estimate was 169%. UBS's 2027 Google Cloud operating margin estimate is 28%, vs 30% before.

UBS EPS estimates (diluted, GAAP): 3Q26E $2.14 (from $2.25, consensus $2.12), 4Q26E $3.44 (from $4.13, consensus $3.18), 2026E $19.78, 2027E $18.28 (consensus $14.96), 2028E $18.86 (consensus $18.08). 1Q26 and 2Q26 EPS were $5.11 and $9.11.
Google guided 2026 capex to about $195-205B and said capex will 'increase significantly in 2027'. UBS now models $340B for 2027 vs $375B before and a Street figure of $328B.
risk_factors: Core Search deceleration, and the risk that AI-driven search monetization does not offset disruption of traditional search.
Google Cloud margin pressure from lower-margin TPU sales and third-party capacity (SpaceX), likely through 1H27.
A very competitive and price-sensitive AI model market, with enterprises routing to cheaper models and open-weight models.
A large capex ramp and negative FCF, with external financing likely in 2027.
Long-term TPU risk from OpenAI's Jalapeno inference chip, plus Nvidia's training lead (CUDA, InfiniBand).
Antitrust and regulatory risk, and risk from scaling Google Cloud profitably, as stated in UBS's risk statement.
Google laps the Wiz acquisition lift in March 2027, a small headwind to Cloud growth.
Power and data-center go-live constraints and political scrutiny of permitting.
charts_described: Figure 2 plots the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index for frontier models: Gemini 4 Argon scored 50, Hydrogen 54 and Carbon 60, while Anthropic's Fable 5.2 scored 65.
Figure 3 shows the AA Coding Agent Index, where Gemini 4 Carbon improved to 55.
Figure 4 shows Artificial Analysis cost per task, where Gemini 4 Carbon is $5.48 per task.
Figure 14 shows record sequential revenue dollar adds for Google Cloud, AWS and Azure, about $13B each in 2Q26 and 3Q26.
vol_and_positioning: Investor sentiment on Alphabet is described as already mixed and cautious, which UBS says limits downside risk.
The stock is down 6% YTD and 26% from its May highs, against a 52-week range of $273.14-$399.04.
UBS says expectations for TPU sales risk becoming too hot, with too little focus on TPU margin pressure.
geopolitical: Post-midterm political and community push-back on data center permitting, which UBS expects to mainly affect new approvals from 2028 on.
Chinese open-weight models (DeepSeek, Kimi, Zhipu, Qwen) face legal and national-security concerns that slow enterprise and US lab adoption.

tension_points.bull_case: Carbon scored 60 on the AA Intelligence Index and 55 on the Coding Agent Index, costs less per task than the leaders, and could win cost-sensitive workloads on cost per successful outcome. Some customers expect Gemini's mix to rise.
tension_points.bear_case: Gemini is a clear #3 in enterprise use. Argon trailed Fable and Astra by 15-25% on frontier workloads, Anthropic's Fable 5.2 (65) has passed Carbon, and Gemini use in the UBS survey fell from 46% to 38%.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Evidence of Gemini share gains with enterprises, or Google recapturing the frontier lead, would challenge the bear case.

tension_points.bull_case: UBS sees $77B of direct TPU sales in 2027 and $125B in 2028 as a material Cloud growth driver, with a structural cost advantage and strong customers including Anthropic and Meta.
tension_points.bear_case: TPU expectations risk being too hot, TPU sales and third-party capacity are margin-dilutive, Nvidia keeps its training lead, and OpenAI's Jalapeno chip is a long-term inference risk.
tension_points.what_invalidates: UBS says it would need far more evidence of strong TPU and Gemini sales to reach the $300B+ Google Cloud revenue some investors assume for 2027.

tension_points.bull_case: Capacity bottlenecks look overdone and Google can fund most capex from operating cash flow, with $265B in cash and securities.
tension_points.bear_case: FCF is negative at -$9B in 3Q26, 2027 capex of $300B+ likely needs external financing, and the build brings a material pending capex ramp.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Capex of $300B or more in 2027 would require Google to tap external financing.

theme_stances.key_argument: Direct TPU sales of $77B in 2027 are a material driver of Google Cloud growth but also likely margin pressure.
theme_stances.evidence: direct sales of TPUs of $77 billion in 2027

theme_stances.key_argument: Google can be competitive but not leading at the frontier, and may win on cheaper models.
Capacity concerns may be overdone, but capex ramp and negative FCF weigh on the stock.
